name: Espresso
shortDescription: A concentrated coffee drink made by forcing hot water through ground coffee under pressure.
fullDescription: Espresso is the base for many drinks on a coffee shop menu. A small serving has a rich flavor, a full body and a layer of golden-brown foam called crema. It can be enjoyed on its own or used as the base for cappuccino, latte and other coffee drinks.
historyAndCulture: Espresso originated in Italy. The first machines that brewed coffee with steam pressure appeared in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and the drink became a symbol of Italian coffee culture: it is drunk quickly, often standing at the bar.
preparationMethod:
Grind the beans finely and tamp the ground coffee in the portafilter.
Start brewing with the espresso machine and extract about 30 ml.
Serve immediately while the crema is still present.

name: Americano
fullDescription: Americano is less concentrated and milder than espresso. You can adjust the amount of water to suit your preferred strength.
historyAndCulture: According to a popular legend, the drink’s name is linked to American soldiers in Italy who diluted espresso with hot water. The story has not been confirmed, so it is best treated as a legend.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Add hot water.
Serve immediately.

name: Cappuccino
shortDescription: Espresso with milk and milk foam.
fullDescription: Cappuccino combines espresso, hot milk and a layer of milk foam. It has a balanced taste in which the coffee and milk complement each other.
historyAndCulture: The name is usually linked to the color of the robes worn by Capuchin friars, which is said to resemble the color of the drink. This explanation is often mentioned in coffee literature.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Froth the milk into a dense warm foam.
Slowly pour the milk into the espresso and spoon the foam on top.

name: Latte
shortDescription: Espresso with plenty of hot milk and a thin layer of foam.
fullDescription: Latte is a milk-forward coffee drink with a mild flavor and considerably more milk than espresso. It is often served in a tall glass or a large cup.
historyAndCulture: The name comes from the Italian caffè latte, meaning “coffee with milk.” In Italian, latte on its own simply means “milk,” so people in Italy usually order a caffè latte.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Warm and lightly froth the milk.
Pour the milk into the espresso, leaving a thin layer of foam on top.

name: Iced latte
shortDescription: A cold latte: espresso, cold milk and ice.
fullDescription: Iced latte is a refreshing version of latte served over ice. You can customize it with a syrup or a plant-based milk.
preparationMethod:
Fill a glass with ice.
Pour in the cold milk.
Add the espresso and, if you like, a syrup. Stir gently.

name: Mocha
shortDescription: Espresso with chocolate and hot milk.
fullDescription: Mocha combines espresso, chocolate and milk. It is a sweet, dessert-like coffee drink similar to a latte with chocolate.
historyAndCulture: The name is associated with the port of Mocha in Yemen, which was historically an important center of the coffee trade.
preparationMethod:
Melt the chocolate in hot milk.
Prepare the espresso.
Combine the chocolate milk with the espresso.

name: Affogato
shortDescription: A scoop of ice cream topped with hot espresso.
fullDescription: Affogato is a simple dessert made with ice cream and espresso, bringing together hot and cold. Serve it immediately, before the ice cream melts.
historyAndCulture: The name comes from the Italian word affogato, meaning “drowned”: the ice cream appears to be “drowned” in espresso.
preparationMethod:
Put a scoop of vanilla ice cream in a glass or cup.
Prepare the espresso.
Pour the espresso over the ice cream and serve immediately.

name: Flat white
shortDescription: A double espresso with smoothly steamed milk and a thin layer of microfoam.
fullDescription: Flat white has a pronounced coffee flavor and a velvety milk texture. It is usually made with a double espresso.
historyAndCulture: Both Australia and New Zealand claim the origin of the drink, so there is no single accepted version.
preparationMethod:
Prepare a double espresso.
Steam the milk until the foam is fine and silky.
Pour the milk into the espresso, leaving a thin layer of microfoam on top.

name: Espresso macchiato
shortDescription: Espresso with a small amount of milk foam.
fullDescription: Macchiato is an espresso topped with a small amount of milk foam. The foam softens the coffee’s flavor slightly without overpowering it.
historyAndCulture: The Italian word macchiato means “marked”: the espresso is marked with a small amount of milk foam.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Froth a little milk.
Spoon a dollop of milk foam on top.

name: Cortado
shortDescription: Espresso with roughly equal parts of warm milk.
fullDescription: Cortado is a small coffee drink in which milk softens the flavor of espresso without overpowering it.
historyAndCulture: The name comes from the Spanish verb cortar, meaning “to cut.” The milk is said to cut through the intensity of the espresso.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Warm the milk without making much foam.
Add the milk to the espresso in roughly equal proportion.

name: Raf coffee
shortDescription: Espresso with cream and a vanilla flavor.
fullDescription: Raf is a sweet, creamy coffee drink made with espresso and cream. It is traditionally flavored with vanilla sugar; this guide recommends vanilla syrup.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Warm the cream with vanilla syrup.
Combine the cream with the espresso and serve immediately.

name: Turkish coffee
shortDescription: Very finely ground coffee brewed in a cezve and served with the grounds.
fullDescription: Turkish coffee has a rich flavor and a full body. It is prepared in a cezve by heating finely ground coffee with cold water. It is sipped slowly, while the grounds settle at the bottom of the cup.
historyAndCulture: The tradition of Turkish coffee was inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.
preparationMethod:
Grind the coffee to a very fine consistency.
Combine the ground coffee, cold water and sugar to taste in a cezve.
Heat over low heat until foam begins to rise. Do not let the mixture boil.
Let the grounds settle, then pour the coffee into cups.

name: Cold brew
shortDescription: Coffee steeped in cold water for many hours.
fullDescription: Cold brew is a smooth, refreshing coffee drink. It is often prepared as a concentrate, which is diluted with water or milk and served over ice.
preparationMethod:
Grind the coffee coarsely and combine it with cold water.
Cover the container and leave it in the refrigerator for about 12–18 hours.
Strain through a paper filter or a fine-mesh sieve.
Dilute the concentrate with water or milk and serve over ice.

name: Espresso tonic
shortDescription: A refreshing drink of espresso, tonic water and ice.
fullDescription: Espresso tonic combines the bittersweet taste of tonic water with the flavor notes of espresso. Light-roasted beans with citrus or fruit-like acidity usually work best.
preparationMethod:
Fill a glass with ice.
Add the tonic water.
Carefully pour the espresso on top so that the layers do not mix immediately.
